atomicClaims.text: The stated optimum is the true maximum cardinality.
The proposed construction lies in [31], has no repeated elements, and has the stated size.
The construction contains exactly three elements of S and no forbidden difference.
The upper-bound argument rules out every larger feasible set.

guardClaims.text: A construction with a duplicate, out-of-range value, forbidden difference, or wrong special count is invalid.
A 15-edge matching on 30 of 31 vertices yields an upper bound of 16, not 15.

validCritiquePredicates.validWhen: The draft gives a different optimum or mishandles the unmatched vertex in the universal upper bound.
The draft construction has the wrong size, special count, range, uniqueness, or a difference of 6 or 10.

verification.method: Check the construction directly. Check that the 15 matching edges are disjoint and each has forbidden difference 6 or 10; they cover 30 vertices, so any feasible set uses at most 15 endpoints plus the unmatched vertex.

atomicClaims.text: The premises are satisfiable.
The query has the same truth value in every satisfying assignment.
There is a satisfying assignment where the query is true and one where it is false.

guardClaims.text: One countermodel disproves entailment but does not by itself prove contradiction.
Both witnesses must satisfy all nine premises under the stated XOR semantics.
A correct OPEN conclusion is a substantive logical result, not model abstention.

validCritiquePredicates.validWhen: The draft says ENTAILED or CONTRADICTED despite a valid opposite-truth witness, or labels OPEN without two valid witnesses.
The draft claims the premise set is inconsistent.

verification.method: Enumerate all 2^10 assignments using the nine stated premises and evaluate (T and Y) implies Q. The four listed assignments are exactly the satisfying models; three make the query true and one false.

atomicClaims.text: The treatment is guaranteed to reduce expected defects from 30.
The supplied marginals determine how many initially defective parts were flagged.
Both improvement and worsening are compatible with the supplied marginals.
The stated final-count range is tight under the supplied constraints.

guardClaims.text: No independence, random sampling, or representative flagging assumption is supplied.
The probabilities determine conditional expected transitions, not the missing joint count.
A correct OPEN conclusion is a substantive answer, not model abstention.

validCritiquePredicates.validWhen: The draft assumes independence or guarantees improvement/worsening without conditioning on x.
The draft gives a different feasible range, formula, overlap bound, or missing statistic.

verification.method: Enumerate integer x in the Frechet interval [max(0,30+35-100), min(30,35)]. Compute 30-0.8x+0.2(35-x)=37-x and confirm both endpoint contingency tables sum to 100.

atomicClaims.text: The current outputs for A, B, C are running, running, interrupted.
The required outputs for A, B, C are completed, interrupted, completed.
Moving the active-run filter before ordinal handling is sufficient to repair every trace.
Ignoring provider-completed for workflow status is sufficient to repair every trace.
Allowing report-verified to overwrite interrupted is sufficient to repair every trace.
A complete repair must address multiple independent scoping, authority, and precedence defects.

guardClaims.text: Moving the run filter alone fixes trace A but not B or C.
Treating provider completion as evidence violates the stated authority boundary.
Arrival order must not override later or earlier verified local evidence.

validCritiquePredicates.validWhen: The draft mis-traces any current or required output.
The draft omits any independent root cause needed by the three traces.
The proposed repair fails a supplied trace, trusts telemetry, or preserves arrival-order-dependent terminal precedence.

verification.method: Execute the supplied projector over all three traces. Compare with a reference facts-first projector; also permute active-run terminal records and require the reference result to remain unchanged.

atomicClaims.text: A local-only protocol can guarantee both at-most-once safety and eventual-application liveness.
Persisting an interrupt intent before calling the provider eliminates every post-send ambiguity.
Retrying whenever no reply was durably recorded preserves the at-most-once safety requirement.
Satisfying both requires a provider-visible idempotency/query capability or relaxing one guarantee.

guardClaims.text: A transactional outbox makes intent durable but cannot atomically include the remote side effect.
Persist-before-send plus never-retry violates liveness when the request is lost.
Persist-before-send plus retry violates at-most-once safety when the first request was applied.

validCritiquePredicates.validWhen: The draft claims a local write or outbox resolves the post-send ambiguity without a provider observation.
The draft silently assumes idempotency, query, history, receipt, a reliable network, or probabilistic success.

verification.method: Explore the finite pre-send/write/send/apply/reply/crash transitions. Pair the two states with identical durable local observations and different provider-applied counts; every recovery policy chooses the same action in both and violates one property.
